x.t: Rescue teams get ready early for the storm Akvan
b: [[andhra-pradesh|Andhra Pradesh]] and Odisha are getting rescue teams ready early. That way, help is close by when the [[cyclone|cyclone]] Akvan arrives.
Fishermen have been told to stay off the sea. In Odisha, people in areas at risk of landslides are to be moved.
On Tuesday, [[imd|India's weather office]] said Akvan was expected to grow stronger. It is expected to cross onto land on Friday. Families can follow updates.

o.t: Akvan forecast to strengthen as rescue teams prepare early
b: [[andhra-pradesh|Andhra Pradesh]] and Odisha are getting national and state disaster response teams into position ahead of [[cyclone|Cyclone]] Akvan, a storm over the [[bay-of-bengal|Bay of Bengal]]. Fishermen have been told not to go to sea.
Odisha's districts have been told to move people from some areas at risk of landslides to relief centres, safe places where people can stay and get help.

In a forecast given on Tuesday, the [[imd|IMD]], India's weather office, said Akvan was expected to become a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening and a very severe cyclonic storm on Thursday 19 November. These are the IMD's names for stronger levels of storm. It is expected to cross the coast onto land between Nellore and Tuni around midday on Friday 20 November, with winds of 120 kilometres an hour or more. Heavy rain is expected in coastal Andhra Pradesh on 19 and 20 November.

stories.think: Why do you think rescue teams are sent out before a storm arrives, instead of after it?

x.t: Some countries do not agree with parts of a climate deal
b: Countries at [[cop|COP31]] in Türkiye are working on a climate deal. Some big groups do not agree with parts of the first [[draft|draft]].
One group includes China and India. It did not agree with a goal for using more electricity. [[minister|Ministers]] are now working on the words so all can agree.
About 30 governments support Türkiye's promise to use more electricity. Joining that promise is a choice, not a rule.

o.t: COP31: big groups of countries object to parts of the first draft
b: The climate talks at [[cop|COP31]] in Antalya, Türkiye, are in their second week. Several big groups of countries have objected to parts of the first [[draft|draft]], an early version of the deal.

One group, the Like-Minded Developing Countries, includes China and India. It objected to a goal for [[electrification|electrification]]: raising electricity's share of the world's energy use to 35%, just over a third, by 2035. It also objected to a roadmap, or plan, for moving away from [[fossil-fuels|fossil fuels]]. Russia and the Arab Group, a group of Arab countries, also objected.

Ministers, senior members of governments, are now working on the text. About 30 governments support Türkiye's voluntary pledge, a promise countries can choose to make, to reach that 35% goal. The final deal needs the backing of nearly 200 countries.

stories.think: When a big group has to agree on one plan and some people object, what is a fair way to find an answer?

x.t: More rare cranes in Ladakh as guards keep their nests safe
b: [[ladakh|Ladakh]] counted 108 black-necked cranes, a kind of bird, in 2026. In 2025 there were only 87. That is nearly a quarter more birds.
These cranes are [[endangered|endangered]], so they are at risk of dying out. Guards keep dogs away from their nests and chicks, to keep them safe.
Local people helped too. Young people were praised for helping to protect wildlife.

o.t: Ladakh's black-necked cranes rise to 108 as guards protect nests
b: [[ladakh|Ladakh]] counted 108 black-necked cranes in 2026, up from 87 in 2025. That is a rise of nearly 25 per cent, or nearly a quarter. Ladakh's administration announced the count on Tuesday.
The black-necked crane is an [[endangered|endangered]] [[species|species]], a kind of animal at risk of dying out. Of the birds counted in 2026, 86 were adults and 22 were juveniles, or young birds.

Ladakh's Lieutenant Governor, the official who leads it, credited guards from the Environment Protection Force, including ex-servicemen, or former members of the armed forces. They protect the cranes' nests and newly hatched chicks from free-ranging dogs, which are dogs that roam freely. Local communities, especially young people, were also praised for taking part in conservation, or work to protect wildlife.

x.t: Leaders of the four Quad countries meet in Manila
b: The [[quad|Quad]] is a group of four countries. They are Australia, India, Japan and the United States. They work together for the [[indo-pacific|Indo-Pacific]] region.
On Tuesday, the four leaders met in Manila, in the Philippines. They met there during the [[asean|ASEAN]] meetings.
India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi called the Quad a trusted partnership. He listed shared work, like keeping seas safe and helping after disasters.

o.t: Quad leaders meet in Manila alongside the ASEAN meetings
b: The leaders of the [[quad|Quad]] met in Manila, the Philippines, on Tuesday 17 November, alongside the meetings of [[asean|ASEAN]], a group of Southeast Asian countries. The Quad is a partnership of four countries: Australia, India, Japan and the United States. They work together for the [[indo-pacific|Indo-Pacific]], the region around the Indian and Pacific Oceans.

The leaders were India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi, US President Donald Trump, Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. Mr Modi said: "For India, the Quad is a constructive and trusted partnership." Constructive means helpful.

Mr Modi listed shared work: maritime security, or keeping the seas safe, and disaster response. He also named new technologies and trusted supply chains, how goods travel from makers to buyers. He said he was confident the meeting would help set "concrete goals for the next phase of our cooperation", meaning specific aims.

local.IN: India is one of the four Quad countries, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi took part in the leaders' meeting in Manila.

stories.think: Why might countries that are far apart choose to work together on things like safe seas or helping after disasters?

b: Karnataka's [[chief-minister|Chief Minister]] D K Shivakumar opened the Bengaluru Tech Summit on Tuesday. It is a big meeting about technology. He said more than 75 countries are taking part.

A [[startup|startup]] is a young company. Karnataka's government will be the first customer for some startups. Its plan is called "Government First". It has set aside Rs 25 crore to buy their products.

o.t: Karnataka sets out plans to help startups at Bengaluru Tech Summit
b: D K Shivakumar, the [[chief-minister|Chief Minister]] of Karnataka, or head of the state's government, opened the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit in Bengaluru on Tuesday 17 November. This year's theme is "AI and Beyond". The Chief Minister said more than 75 countries are taking part, up from 57 last year.

Under a plan called "Government First", the state government will become the first customer for some [[startup|startups]], or young companies. It has set aside Rs 25 crore to buy new products and ideas that these startups develop. The Chief Minister said Karnataka has more than 24,000 recognised startups.

The state government also plans a government-led AI University. [[ai|AI]], short for artificial intelligence, means computers that can do tasks that usually need human intelligence. An AI Hub would be at the centre of the university, bringing startups, researchers and industry together.

x.t: How to spot shooting stars after midnight tonight
b: The Leonid [[meteor|shooting stars]] are at their best tonight. In a very dark place, you might see up to about 15 an hour.
These shooting stars are made by tiny bits of dust from a [[comet|comet]]. They zoom into our air and glow as they burn up.
Look from midnight until dawn, with a grown-up. Find a safe, dark spot, away from lights. No telescope is needed.

o.t: The Leonid meteor shower peaks tonight: how to see it
b: The Leonid [[meteor|meteor]] shower peaks on the night of Tuesday 17 November into Wednesday 18 November. A meteor, or shooting star, is the streak of light made when a tiny bit of space dust burns up in Earth's air. In ideal dark skies there can be up to about 15 an hour, though most people will see fewer.

The dust comes from a [[comet|comet]] called 55P/Tempel-Tuttle and enters our air at about 70 kilometres a second. The meteors seem to come from the constellation Leo, a group of stars that forms a pattern.

The Moon sets before the best viewing time, so its light should not get in the way. Watch from after midnight until dawn, away from lights. No telescope is needed, but give your eyes about 30 minutes to get used to the dark.

stories.think: Why do you think it helps to watch for shooting stars from a dark place, away from lights?

quiz.q: Where does the dust that makes the Leonid shooting stars come from?

o.t: Fisherman and carpenter Nicholas Herring wins the Giller Prize
b: Nicholas Herring, an author from Prince Edward Island in Canada who works as a fisherman and a carpenter, has won Canada's Giller Prize. The winner was announced on Monday 16 November in Toronto. Herring receives $100,000 for his [[novel|novel]], a long made-up story, called Your Breath in Charcoal.
The book follows an everyman named Knickle on a road trip. An everyman is an ordinary person who stands for lots of ordinary people. The prize's [[jury|jury]], the group of judges, praised the book.

Five books reached the last round of the prize. The four other [[finalist|finalists]], the writers whose books made it to that last stage, were Tara Gereaux, Michelle Good, Nazanine Hozar and Patmeena Sabit. Each of them receives $10,000, so every finalist is rewarded, not only the winner.

born.name: August Ferdinand Möbius
born.what: A German mathematician and astronomer, born in Schulpforta, Saxony. In 1848 he became director of the observatory at Leipzig. In 1858 he discovered the Möbius strip, a surface with only one side. Another mathematician, Johann Benedict Listing, discovered it at about the same time.

born.name: Eugene Wigner
born.what: A physicist born in Budapest, Hungary, who became a citizen of the United States in 1937. He won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1963. He taught at Princeton University from 1938 until he retired in 1971.

o.t: How do cyclones get their names?
b: A tropical cyclone is a spinning storm that forms over the ocean. The same kind of storm is called a hurricane in the North Atlantic, a typhoon in the western North Pacific and a cyclone in the Indian Ocean.

Storms in the north Indian Ocean take their names from a list made by 13 countries, including India. The list has 169 names. Each country gave 13 names. A storm gets its name when its winds reach 62 kilometres an hour. The name is given by the India Meteorological Department, India's weather office.
A name helps people remember a storm. It also avoids confusion when two storms are active at the same time. Each name is used only once. Akvan is one of the names given by Iran.
o.remember: Cyclones in the north Indian Ocean are named from a list of 169 names given by 13 countries, and each name is used only once.

backThen.t: The first robot rover lands on the Moon
backThen.o: On 17 November 1970, the Soviet spacecraft Luna 17 landed on the Moon, in a region called the Sea of Rains. Luna 17 was launched on 10 November 1970. It carried Lunokhod 1, the first remote-controlled robot rover on the Moon. Lunokhod 1 had eight wheels. A team on Earth drove it by remote control. It carried television cameras. It kept working for many months.
backThen.x: On this day in 1970, a robot rover landed on the Moon. Its name was Lunokhod 1. It had eight wheels. People on Earth drove it by remote control.
backThen.why: Lunokhod 1 showed that people on Earth could drive a robot on another world. In 2010, scientists bounced laser pulses from Earth off the old rover's reflector.

hiddenWords.o: Cyclone comes from the Greek word kyklos, which means circle.
Robot comes from the Czech word robota, which means forced labour.

days.o: NASA launched Voyager 1 on 5 September 1977. It flew past Jupiter in 1979 and Saturn in 1980, and in 1990 it took a picture of Earth known as the Pale Blue Dot. In 2012 it entered interstellar space, the space between the stars. It is run from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California.
days.x: Voyager 1 is a spacecraft. It left Earth in 1977. It flew past the planets Jupiter and Saturn. In 1990 it took a picture of Earth from very far away.

days.o: A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, about 25.9 billion kilometres. Light reaches the Moon in about 1.3 seconds, and sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. After sunset today, Tuesday 17 November, NASA invites people to flash VGR, Voyager's three-letter call sign, in Morse code towards the sky with a torch.
